arxiv-2101-00779.title: The ( t − 1 ) (t-1) -chromatic Ramsey number for paths
arxiv-2101-00779.creator: Matija Bucić Amir Khamseh
arxiv-2101-00779.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Matija Bucić Amir Khamseh. The following relaxation of the classical problem of determining Ramsey number of a fixed graph has first been proposed by Erdős, Hajnal and Rado over 50 years ago. Given a graph G G and an integer t ≥ 2 t\geq 2 determine the minimum number N N such that in any t t -coloured complete graph on N N vertices there is a copy of G G using only edges of some t − 1 t-1 colours.

arxiv-2104-01632.title: Isconna: Streaming Anomaly Detection with Frequency and Patterns
arxiv-2104-01632.creator: Rui Liu, Siddharth Bhatia, Bryan Hooi
arxiv-2104-01632.description: Abstract An edge stream is a common form of presentation of dynamic networks. It can evolve with time, with new types of nodes or edges being continually added. Existing methods for anomaly detection rely on edge occurrence counts or compare pattern snippets found in historical records.

arxiv-2205-14306.title: Multipartite Entanglement in the Random Ising Chain
arxiv-2205-14306.creator: Jay S. Zou, Helen S. Ansell, István A. Kovács
arxiv-2205-14306.description: Abstract Quantifying entanglement of multiple subsystems is a challenging open problem in interacting quantum systems. Here, we focus on two subsystems of length ℓ \ell separated by a distance r = α ​ ℓ r=\alpha\ell and quantify their entanglement negativity ( ℰ {\cal E} ) and mutual information ( ℐ {\cal I} ) in critical random Ising chains.

arxiv-2404-07271.title: Cautionary tales on heating-rate prescriptions in kilonovae
arxiv-2404-07271.creator: Nikhil Sarin, Stephan Rosswog
arxiv-2404-07271.description: Abstract A major ingredient for kilonova lightcurves is the radioactive heating rate and its dependence on the electron fraction and velocity of the ejecta and, in principle, on the nuclear mass formula. Heating-rate formulae commonly used as the basis for kilonova models previously employed in the literature produce substantially different outputs for high electron fractions ( Y e ≳ 0.

arxiv-2404-14921.title: More Church-Rosser Proofs in Beluga
arxiv-2404-14921.creator: Alberto Momigliano, Martina Sassella
arxiv-2404-14921.description: Abstract We report on yet another formalization of the Church-Rosser property in lambda-calculi, carried out with the proof environment Beluga . After the well-known proofs of confluence for β \beta -reduction in the untyped settings, with and without Takahashi’s complete developments method, we concentrate on η \eta -reduction and obtain the result for β ​ η \beta\eta modularly.

arxiv-2502-15550.title: On the quantum parameter in the quantum cohomology of a family of odd symplectic partial flag varieties
arxiv-2502-15550.creator: Connor Bean, Caleb Shank, Ryan M. Shifler
arxiv-2502-15550.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Connor Bean, Caleb Shank, Ryan M. Shifler. We will consider a particular family of odd symplectic partial flag varieties denoted by IF \mathrm{IF} . In the quantum cohomology ring QH ∗ ​ ( IF ) \mathrm{QH}^{*}(\mathrm{IF}) , we will show that q 1 q 2 ⋯ q m q_{1}q_{2}\cdots q_{m} appears m m times in the quantum product τ D ​ i ​ v i ⋆ τ i ​ d \tau_{Div_{i}}\star\tau_{id} when expressed as a sum in terms of the Schubert basis.

arxiv-2506-10016.title: A Survey of Generative Categories and Techniques in Multimodal Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-10016.creator: Longzhen Han, Awes Mubarak, Almas Baimagambetov, Nikolaos Polatidis, Thar Baker
arxiv-2506-10016.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Longzhen Han, Awes Mubarak, Almas Baimagambetov, Nikolaos Polatidis, Thar Baker. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have rapidly evolved beyond text generation, now spanning diverse output modalities including images, music, video, human motion, and 3D objects, by integrating language with other sensory modalities under unified architectures. This survey categorises six primary generative modalities and examines how foundational techniques, namely Self-Supervised Learning (SSL), Mixture of Experts (MoE), Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, enable cross-modal capabilities.

arxiv-2511-12490.title: Discovery of a 13-Sharpe OOS Factor: Drift Regimes Unlock Hidden Cross-Sectional Predictability
arxiv-2511-12490.creator: Mainak Singha
arxiv-2511-12490.description: Abstract We document an high cross-sectional equity factor achieving out-of-sample Sharpe ratios exceeding 13 through regime-conditional signal activation. By combining value and short-term reversal signals exclusively during stock-specific drift regimes—periods when individual stocks exhibit over 60% positive days in trailing 63-day windows—we generate annualized returns of 158.6% with 12.0% volatility and maximum drawdown of − 11.9 % -11.9\% .

arxiv-2511-16735.title: Adiabatic reverse annealing is robust to low-temperature decoherence
arxiv-2511-16735.creator: An Le, Christopher Baldwin
arxiv-2511-16735.description: Abstract Adiabatic reverse annealing (ARA) is an improvement to conventional quantum annealing (QA) that uses an initial guess at the desired ground state to circumvent problematic phase transitions. Despite encouraging results in the closed-system setting, Ref. Passarelli et al. 2022 has suggested on the basis of numerical simulations that ARA may lose its advantage in the presence of decoherence.

arxiv-2601-11811.title: Do Boxes Affect Exploration Behavior and Performance in Group-in-a-box Layouts?
arxiv-2601-11811.creator: Yuki Ueno, Hiroaki Natsukawa, Koji Koyamada
arxiv-2601-11811.description: Abstract The group-in-a-box (GIB) layout is an efficient graph drawing method designed to visualize the group structure of graphs. The layout communicates group sizes and both within-group and between-group network structures simultaneously. The layout is characterized by its composition of multiple elements, including nodes, edges, and boxes. However, there is limited empirical guidance on how these elements should be combined.

pmc-10558030.title: Perspective-Taking and Perspective-Sharing in Pediatric Education: Exploring Connections Between Strategies of Medical Students and Patients’ Caregivers
pmc-10558030.creator: M C L Eijkelboom, R A M de Kleijn, L Baten, J Frenkel, M F van der Schaaf
pmc-10558030.description: Introduction:In pediatric education, caregivers are increasingly involved to share their perspective. Yet, an in-depth understanding of the perspective-taking process between medical students and caregivers is lacking. This study explored: 1) Which strategies do medical students use to take a caregiver’s perspective and which facilitators and constraints do they perceive?

pmc-10706619.title: Characterization of Lactic Acid Bacteria and Yeast from Grains as Starter Cultures for Gluten-Free Sourdough
pmc-10706619.creator: Seung-Hye Woo, Jiwoon Park, Jung Min Sung, Eun-Ji Choi, Yun-Sang Choi, Jong-Dae Park, João Miguel F Rocha
pmc-10706619.description: With the increasing number of people affected by gluten consumption-related diseases, adhering to a gluten-free (GF) diet is the most effective preventive measure. Herein, we aimed to isolate and characterize the functional properties of autochthonous lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and yeast from various GF sourdoughs to determine their suitability in starter cultures for sourdough preparation.

pmc-11643377.title: Adherence to the Cancer Prevention Recommendations from World Cancer Research Fund/American Institute for Cancer Research After Cancer Diagnosis on Mortality in South Korea
pmc-11643377.creator: Donghyun Won, Jeeyoo Lee, Sooyoung Cho, Ji Yoon Baek, Daehee Kang, Aesun Shin, Alessandro Granito
pmc-11643377.description: Background/Objectives: The World Cancer Research Fund/American Institute for Cancer Research recommends following the recommendations for cancer prevention even after cancer diagnosis. To provide evidence on the potential benefits of adherence on improved survival, we investigated the effects of post-diagnostic adherence to the recommendations regarding diet, physical activity, and body weight on all-cause mortality among Korean cancer survivors.

pmc-12443488.title: Efficacy of Atezolizumab, Bevacizumab, Carboplatin, and Paclitaxel Therapy in Patients With Genetic Alterations in Non‐Small Cell Lung Cancer
pmc-12443488.creator: Tsunehiro Tanaka, Motohiro Tamiya, Akito Miyazaki, Kiyohide Komura, Shun Futamura, Takahisa Kawamura, Kei Kunimasa, Takako Inoue, Kazumi Nishino
pmc-12443488.description: BackgroundThe IMpower150 trial demonstrated the efficacy of atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatin, and paclitaxel (ABCP) therapy in epidermal growth factor receptor ( EGFR )‐mutated non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, its efficacy in patients with NSCLC harboring other genetic alterations in real‐world settings remains unclear.

pmc-12579598.title: Modeling and addressing on-target/off-tumor toxicity of claudin 18.2 targeted immunotherapies
pmc-12579598.creator: Elizabeth J. Carstens, Kazuki Takahashi, Naoya Sakamoto, Martina De Vizio, Micaela Morgado, Shahryar Khoshtinat Nikkhoi, Abhishek Mangipudi, Canh Hiep Nguyen, Tate Weltzin, Izuma Nakayama, Qiang Lv, Jue Zeng, Cui Nie, Changjing Deng, Xiaoxiao Wang, Lile Liu, Samuel J. Klempner, Anusuya Ramasubramani
pmc-12579598.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Successfully extending immunotherapies to solid tumors involves addressing several key challenges, importantly the “antigen dilemma”, the expression of a solid tumor target antigen on the normal tissue of tumor origin. Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2) has emerged as an important target for upper gastrointestinal (GI) cancer therapies (such as Zolbetuximab, a naked antibody, recently approved; or CT041, a second-generation chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy with promising clinical data). However, GI toxicities are reported from clinical use of both Zolbetuximab and CT041.

pmc-12607132.title: Unravelling butyrate metabolism in sepsis: identification of key genes
pmc-12607132.creator: Yeyan Zhu, Fang Tian, Fan Ge, Yue Wang, Jingxian Lu, Haiqi Zhou, Qixiang Yan, Yingfang Zhang, Jiang Zhou, Jun Lu
pmc-12607132.description: BackgroundSepsis is an infection-induced systemic inflammatory response. Given the potential link between changes in butyrate metabolism (BM) and sepsis development, this study aimed to preliminarily identify potential BM-related genes and explore their possible relevance to sepsis treatment strategies.MethodsThe GSE54514, GSE175453 and GSE65682 datasets, as well as BM-related genes (BMRGs), were obtained from public databases.

pmc-12812756.title: Proteomic analysis confirmed that the occurrence of diabetic sarcopenia is related to autophagy and apoptosis
pmc-12812756.creator: Tianrui Wang, Liang Zhang, Yu Jiang, Xia Zhao, Kehao Hou, Yingze Zhang, Ning Yu, Kuishuai Xu
pmc-12812756.description: ObjectiveMore and more evidence indicates that type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) can cause muscle lesions and lead to the occurrence of sarcopenia. The changes in the gastrocnemius muscle of T2DM rats were investigated by using tandem mass tag (TMT) proteomics technology, with the aim of discovering biomarkers of muscle lesions induced by T2DM and clarifying their potential biological relationships.

pmc-12986123.title: Evaluation of an ESAT-6 Recombinant Skin Test Reagent for Bovine Tuberculosis Diagnosis in Guinea Pigs and Cattle
pmc-12986123.creator: Matías Iván Gatto, Sol Ferrero, Florencia Tonini, Marcela Desio, Gerardo Rodríguez, Fernando Martino, Bernardo Alonso, Claudio Paolazzi, Claudia Argüelles, Gustavo Helguera
pmc-12986123.description: Bovine purified protein derivative (PPD-B), a crude protein extract from Mycobacterium bovis cultures, has been the standard reagent for delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) testing in cattle, but its undefined composition and variability compromise reproducibility and specificity. To address these limitations, we developed and evaluated RRbTB-E, a recombinant fusion protein comprising ESAT-6, as a defined alternative for skin testing.

pmc-13264916.creator: Xiaoting Wang, Shumin Wu, Liying Zhang

pmc-13373191.creator: Misara M. Awad, Ahmed A. Abdelrahman, Ahmed A. Abdel-Aal, Ibrahim M. Hassan, Seham M. El-Marakby
pmc-13373191.description: This study investigated the ability of low doses to cause an in vivo radio-adaptive response (RAR) and examined the biological effects of acute low-dose total-body gamma irradiation in rats. Adult male rats were randomly divided into 8 groups. Acute gamma radiation doses of 0.25, 0.5, and 0.

pmc-13414566.title: SPARC family proteins: matricellular modulators of cancer progression and therapeutic resistance
pmc-13414566.creator: Rachel Huey Xuan Hoe, Thamil Selvee Ramasamy, Ajantha Sinniah, Ain Zubaidah Ayob
pmc-13414566.description: The SPARC (secreted protein acidic and rich in cysteine) family represents a unique class of matricellular proteins – including SPARC, SPARCL1, SPOCK1-3, SMOC1-2, and FSTL1 – that regulate extracellular matrix (ECM) dynamics, cell signaling, and tissue homoeostasis. In cancer, their expression is frequently dysregulated, through epigenetic mechanisms, microRNAs, and interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME).

pmc-13425607.title: Effects of Cereal Byproducts on Antioxidant Capacity of Black Soldier Fly Oil
pmc-13425607.creator: Yung‐Sheng Lin, Yu‐Ting Zhu, Cheng‐Kun He, Cheng‐You Chen, Chin‐Tung Wu

pmc-13458100.title: Posterior Bony Bankart Bridge and Reverse Remplissage in an Elite Contact Athlete
pmc-13458100.creator: Ayham Jaber, Tyler J. Uppstrom, Michael Nocek, Colin P. Murphy, Taylor K. Calibo, Peter J. Millett
pmc-13458100.description: Background:Posterior or multidirectional shoulder instability are common among athletes subjected to repetitive posterior loading. Posterior glenohumeral dislocation can result in a posterior bony Bankart lesion, which presents a unique challenge in arthroscopic repair.Indications:Surgical repair is considered for patients with high physical demands and for those with instability refractory to nonoperative treatment, as observed in this 21-year-old professional hockey player.

pmc-13659211.title: Modulation of hormones in perimenopausal women by probiotics associated by specific gut bacteria: a pilot study
pmc-13659211.creator: Sara Julietta Lozano Herrera, Tania Aguilar López, Niko Alain Cruz Sancen, Nataly García Gutiérrez, Haydé Azeneth Vergara Castañeda, Diego Iván Morales Hernandez
pmc-13659211.description: IntroductionPerimenopause is characterised by hormonal fluctuations that can affect metabolism. Recent studies suggest that the gut microbiota, which can be regulated by taking probiotics, influences hormone regulation. One proposed mechanism is the activity of β-glucuronidase, which hydrolyzes excreted hormones, allowing them to be reabsorbed.
